stem: How can a clinician best differentiate benign sleep myoclonus from jitteriness in a neonate?

options.text: Benign sleep myoclonus will stop immediately if the limb is passively flexed.
Jitteriness occurs primarily during deep sleep, whereas sleep myoclonus occurs when awake.
Benign sleep myoclonus disappears abruptly when the child is awakened.
Jitteriness is always associated with an abnormal EEG, while sleep myoclonus is not.

explanation: A defining feature of benign sleep myoclonus is that it only occurs during sleep and ceases instantly upon arousal.
rationale: Focus on what happens to the movements when the child's state of consciousness changes.

optionExplanations.A: It is actually jitteriness that stops with passive flexion; benign sleep myoclonus persists despite such maneuvers.
optionExplanations.B: Jitteriness occurs in wakefulness, while benign sleep myoclonus is strictly limited to sleep.
optionExplanations.C: A defining feature of benign sleep myoclonus is that it only occurs during sleep and ceases instantly upon arousal.
optionExplanations.D: Both jitteriness and benign sleep myoclonus are typically associated with a normal EEG.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Benign sleep myoclonus disappears abruptly when the child is awakened.
